en: At that time, when [the Bodhisattva] was driving forth the mind of the Great Way according to the nature of reality (*dharmatā*), the Tathāgata was seated upon a lion throne beneath the Bhagavati tree on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.

There was an assembly of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas, all of whom were consecrated (*abhiṣikta*) and had turned back from non-retrogression (*avaivartika*). Their names were...
His stature was as lofty as Mount Sumeru;
he circumambulated the Buddha four hundred thousand times and then sat down in silence.
At that time, the Bodhisattva was traveling through various countries to teach and transform sentient beings.
He arrived at the foot of Mount Vipula and went to the house of the elder Gṛhapati.
Within the house of that elder, various malevolent spirits had seized his vital essence.
There were five hundred people in the household,
all of whom lay unconscious and unresponsive.
After ten days had passed,
the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, having witnessed these events,
immediately formed this thought:
How truly bitter! How truly painful!
There are such unspeakable matters in the world.
Out of compassion for these sentient beings, I act as their savior.
As he spoke these words,
he immediately leaped into the air and went to Vulture Peak to the place where the Tathāgata was;
there he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times.
Stepping back to one side, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I have recently been traveling through various kingdoms to teach and transform sentient beings,
until I arrived at the foot of Mount Vipula."
He saw that in the house of the elder Ghoṭamukha,
there were more than five hundred people,
all of whom had their vital energy drained by malevolent spirits.
He lay unconscious on the ground for several days.
Having seen this, I gave rise to a heart of compassion and a heart of protective affection.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will permit me to speak this method of deliverance,
so that all malevolent spirits may be subdued by humans,
and all practitioners may employ them at will.
He further caused the elder to recover as he was before.
At that time, the World-Honored One emitted light ten thousand fathoms long from the tuft of hair upon his crown,
illuminating the body of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva, knowing the Tathāgata’s intention, was granted permission to proclaim [the teaching].
Then, the members of the great assembly said to one another:
"Today the Tathāgata has emitted light that illuminates the Bodhisattva’s body."
"This bodhisattva will surely achieve the Great Dharma to transform and teach sentient beings.
At that time, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva rose from his seat,
approached the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
World-Honored One, from the past until now, I have received the Buddha’s instruction.
Today, once again before the Tathāgata, I shall speak this brief teaching to enable all sentient beings to be free from the entanglements of the five hindrances.
Furthermore, one shall attain peace and security within the world, free from all decline and affliction.
World-Honored One, I now possess a divine mantra capable of removing depraved thoughts.
Furthermore, it can command all malevolent spirits and the like,
causing all sentient beings to attain complete understanding.
If a practitioner is afflicted by various demons, [this mantra shall protect them].
One should practice this Dharma of mine without deviation.
If one wishes to command any spirits or deities,
they shall each fulfill whatever is required according to one's will.
If one recites this mantra and practices this rite for three days and three nights, one shall attain accomplishment.
World-Honored One, if there are those who resolve to employ [this method] to dispel and eliminate calamities and misfortunes, [they shall succeed].
One who wishes to know future events,
as well as the supernormal knowledge of past lives and natural wisdom—
possessing these three.
Furthermore, it causes those who are not yet united to be united,
and those who are not yet settled to be settled.
World-Honored One, this Dharma is able to fully possess immeasurable wisdom.
One will be able to possess immeasurable power.
Whether a practitioner is a householder or one who has left the home life,
wherever they may dwell, there is nothing that will not be accomplished through the practice of this dharma.
“World-Honored One, in the past, immeasurable, boundless, and long ago,
there was a Buddha named King Lamp-Light (Dīpamkara-rāja).
That Buddha was fully endowed with the ten titles.”
I also teach and transform sentient beings by means of the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
during the period of the Semblance Dharma, I shall abide in the stage of an ordinary person.
There was a rishi on Mount Kūṭaka who was well-versed in the arts of the Way.
I saw sentient beings being tormented by various evil spirits,
just as in that householder’s home;
at that time, I made this vow:
"I pray that I may meet a spiritual friend who can teach me the method for subduing [the demon].
Having spoken these words,
he immediately went to Kūṭatāla to seek out that rishi.
Seeing me, joy arose in his heart,
and he immediately questioned me regarding the methods of that seer.
At that time, the seer caused me to attain understanding over the course of three days.
One must know that news of good and evil from ten thousand li away will arrive.
Furthermore, all malevolent spirits will gather at my location;
I shall subdue their minds according to the teachings of the Master’s Dharma and cause them to resolve upon the Way.
Furthermore, as this mantra was recited,
in an instant all sentient beings suffering in the various hells each received a lotus flower,
and their sufferings were brought to a halt.
At that time, the rishi, seeing that I had attained such supernatural powers,
bestowed upon me a prophecy, saying:
"In immeasurable and boundless worlds to come..."
The Buddha bestowed upon him a prophecy of enlightenment,
naming him Kṣitigarbha,
for the sake of humans and devas in this world of the five turbidities and hardships.
Kṣitigarbha constantly manifests emanations to rescue and deliver sentient beings, enabling them to emerge from their entanglements.
That seer bestowed a prophecy upon me;
therefore, I shall further refine my diligence and practice this Dharma.
Now, seeing that the elder is no different from before,
if a practitioner of the path performs this rite,
they may consult and receive instruction as they wish.
When I went to that place to compile their records,
all the ghosts manifested themselves simultaneously and were dispatched according to my will.
"It shall be exactly as I have performed the ritual, without any difference. Having spoken these words,
the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha then recited a mantra before the Buddha, saying:
"Namaḥ nārāyaṇāya kṛupamatsyatuṃbaṃ svāhā. Having spoken this mantra, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, whenever one wishes to perform a ritual rite..."
First, take five kinds of exquisite incense:
first, one *liang* of white sandalwood; second, one *liang* of breast-milk resin; third, one *liang* of clove; fourth, one *liang* of *śrīkhaṇḍa*; and fifth, one *liang* of the hundred-fold compound.
Take the five kinds of excellent incense mentioned above,
grind them finely, and mix them with white honey.
Regarding each of these perfumes, one must not purchase them from the market nor smell them at will.
To remove impurities and make it fragrant, he said:
"Recite my name. Having finished blending the incense, he spoke thus.
Either within one's own room,
or in a clear field at dawn,
or on a high plateau.
Simply dwell wherever the practitioner finds pleasure.
Perform the ritual to take seven feet of pure cloth and seven cups of milk gruel;
place them upon the pure cloth.
Take a white porcelain incense burner.
This incense summons all the spirits;
their names are Nalasu and Nalasu.
Repeat these words three times,
calling out the name each time; having finished the three invocations,
recite the mantra three hundred times.
Before performing the ritual,
one must not recite the text at random even once.
Once the three invocations have been completed with three hundred recitations, [the rite may proceed].
Next, recite the mantra two hundred times and summon [the deity] three times as before.
Furthermore, recite it one hundred times and likewise summon [the deity] three times.
This continued for three days up to the third repetition;
every night it was done in this manner.
At other times, one should simply recite the name of Kṣitigarbha.
World-Honored One, as for that Dharma, on the first day there is one sign:
a cloud of extraordinary color arises from the crown of the head, accompanied by an extraordinary fragrance.
On the second day, there appeared in the sky a lotus flower made of a hundred jewels and a manifestation of a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*).
On the third day, there was a great wind and the sound of bells arose from both [the sky and the earth].
If a practitioner sees such signs,
it must be that various devas have lent them their majestic power;
at that time, all the ghosts and spirits of the world [will likewise assist].
They all gathered like clouds, filling the void of space;
the practitioner knew for himself that the various spirits had arrived,
yet he was not yet able to see them clearly.
When one wishes to see [the deity],
one should recite the mantra one hundred or two hundred times according to the three preceding methods;
then the form will manifest subtly, though not yet clearly.
At that time, the Bodhisattva immediately performed the rite for fearlessness regarding the sight of spirits.
World-Honored One, when a person who practices this rite has gathered the spirits and wishes to cause them to appear:
Take clear water and sprinkle it toward the ghosts.
Then, form the *duśe* mudrā:
first slightly lift the left foot while keeping the right foot standing upright.
Bend the left thumb;
with the palm, press down upon the knuckle of the index finger.
Form a fist with the right hand and let it hang downward.
He immediately summoned them by their names, calling out three times;
the ghosts all arrived and manifested their forms,
causing people to feel terrified.
At that moment, he immediately recited the aforementioned mantra once and pointed it toward the ghost;
both sat in silence, without speaking a word.
If one wishes to cause ghosts and spirits who see one's body to be free from fear,
one should perform the Seal of Compassionate Rescue and Gathering.
As before, slightly bend the left leg.
Interlace the left and right hands with the palms joined;
thus one will be free from fear and dread.
Having performed this rite, one may then converse with the spirit.
Knock the teeth three or five times.
Then, opening the mouth wide, speak these words with a loud voice:
"Tut! Tut!"
"Who are you that have come here?
I possess a divine spell capable of eliminating evil spirits;
if it does not eliminate or subjugate them,"
In an instant, he died.
"Alas! Alas!"—these were the words spoken at that time.
The ghosts fell face-down in terror;
with single-minded right mindfulness, each abandoned their perverse thoughts and recited these words three times.
The ghost confessed his capital offense.
The World-Honored One felt compassion for that spirit’s fear;
once it had been subdued, he immediately caused it to rejoice.
Form the mudrā of fearlessness:
with both feet together, let the right hand hang down,
and bend the left hand upward at the heart.
Bend the little finger and the ring finger toward the palm;
press their joints with the thumb.
Recite the name [of the deity] three times according to the previous invocation.
That ghost immediately approached the traveler and spoke these words:
"O Great Being, I am a ghost.
My retribution is extremely heavy; I constantly harass and disturb all beings."
They constantly seek out the shortcomings of others and perpetually devour the blood-veins of sentient beings,
never ceasing for even a moment.
"May this Bodhisattva, by means of such majestic power, have brought me here and caused me to resolve upon the path to enlightenment.
Even if I were to shatter this body into fine dust,
it would still be difficult to exhaust my gratitude for the Bodhisattva's kindness."
"I only pray that the Great Being will explain for me the method for extinguishing sins and transforming this evil body.
May the practitioner, according to their wishes, act for the sake of the Buddha-dharma so that awakening and understanding may be attained.
Upon hearing this teaching, the ghost gave rise to a heart of joy.
Then, together with the practitioner, he speaks of worldly matters and teaches sentient beings;
he fulfills their wishes according to their desires.
After a brief moment, the practitioner speaks and he departs.
"You all, you ghosts, must be careful not to [be negligent].
Together with you, I shall always be a virtuous friend who saves sentient beings,
according to whatever each sentient being’s mind desires."
"We shall give it to you together.
He spoke again:
"If there are sentient beings who seek various kinds of knowledge and various dhāraṇīs and arts..."
We shall go with you to that place of instruction;
there, you may inquire as you wish and we shall satisfy you completely.
If there are sentient beings who undergo various forms of suffering and calamity in their bodies, [we shall provide relief].
If there are sentient beings whose bodies are subjected to execution by kings or officials;
or if there are sentient beings afflicted by the calamities of water or fire;
or those beset by wicked birds and beasts, venomous dragons, vengeful bandits, or thieves.
"In matters such as these, I shall go with you to rescue them and bring about their liberation.
Whatever they require, I shall joyfully bestow as gifts so that they may attain peace and happiness.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner wishes to command the yakṣas..."
When vermilion is used to write these talismans,
they will subsequently cause the three seals to swallow the nine provinces of the world.
Thereafter, one performs the rite to command ghosts to act with speed and dispatch them everywhere.
[The text is] missing one hundred characters.
World-Honored One, if you would cause the spirits to know how many years, months, and days after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa he will pass away, and in what place he will enter extinction.
Regarding the knowledge of future events:
one summons a spirit and asks; in an instant, it reports everything so that all is known.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner employs a spirit, they can cause it to know the events of the three periods of time.
He summoned the spirit and questioned it; in an instant, the spirit reported whether the matter was favorable or unfavorable.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner is harmed or slandered by an evil person, they should summon the spirit and converse with it.
Those who are targeted by human officials or those who conspire to harm them shall all suffer from the afflictions of non-human spirits. Furthermore,
World-Honored One, those who uphold the Dharma and are surrounded by malevolent birds and beasts seeking to harm their bodies [shall likewise be protected].
He summoned the spirits and spoke with them;
the heads of the fierce beasts and others were split into seven pieces.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner enters the great ocean to gather treasures...
When various evil venomous dragons, fierce beasts, tortoises, and crocodiles intended to come and cause harm,
he summoned the spirits and spoke with them;
consequently, all those fierce beasts sank into the mud and did not emerge again.
World-Honored One, regarding those practitioners who have been cursed, suppressed, or bound by others:
by reciting these characters and pointing toward the five paths of rebirth, one may announce their vows to Heaven and Earth,
and summon spirits to converse with them.
In an instant, those wicked people and their captors found their mouths bound;
blood flowed from their eyes and great serpents emerged from their ears,
while their hands and feet involuntarily contracted.
Furthermore, there was a great serpent coiled around him;
he suffered such agony that the World-Honored One desired to release him.
Summon the spirits and speak with them, commanding them to release [the victim]. Then they will say:
"Swiftly, *svalu-li*.
Once these words have been spoken, [the victim] shall immediately be released.
World-Honored One, if there are enemies, thieves, or spies seeking to harm those who uphold this Dharma,
they may summon spirits and converse with them;
yet on that very day, those spirits shall be bound and brought back to the person practicing this rite.
If one wishes to summon a spirit and speak with it, one will immediately attain liberation.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner during a time of famine summons a spirit and speaks with it,
that spirit can procure food from the five directions and worlds to give to the practitioner to eat.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner, during a time of pestilence, [is protected by] the spirits and deities,
then among people there will be no difference in their longevity;
they will remain exactly as they were, without the slightest variation.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner, when their body is being consumed by the kalpa-fire,
summons a spirit and converses with it,
they will attain refreshing coolness and the fire will be unable to harm them.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner is being swept away by water and calls upon spirits to converse with them,
a lotus flower made of a hundred jewels will spring up from the earth.
When a practitioner of the Dharma encounters the calamity of floods in another world,
World-Honored One, if a person suffers from demonic possession and someone summons a spirit to speak with that person...
If [the patient] is such a person, when the *pishāca* spirits go to the place of the sick person,
they will be cured immediately upon reciting the aforementioned mantra seven times.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner treats one suffering from *vilina* disease, [they should act as follows].
He summoned a spirit and questioned it.
If the condition could be cured, one should take a handful of *pài* branches,
boil them, and take one *hé*.
If one recites the mantra seven times and administers it to the patient, they will recover immediately.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner treats various kinds of wind-diseases,
they should summon the spirit and question it.
Consecrated water is given for the practitioner to drink.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner treats various kinds of afflictions by summoning spirits and interrogating them,
and consecrated water is given for them to drink, they will recover immediately.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner treats the eyes for various forms of blindness and darkness— whether one has sight or not—
they summon spirits and question them.
For those who can be cured, take one *harītakī* fruit,
crush it, mix it with breast milk,
and apply it as a drop to the eyes.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times;
on the third day, the patient shall recover.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner treats those afflicted by illnesses caused by malevolent spirits, [they shall be cured].
He summoned a spirit and questioned it.
As soon as the incantation was completed, [the patient] was immediately cured.
The World-Honored One then recounted the origins of that multitude... [text missing].
Though it would be difficult to exhaust [this teaching] even through the end of an eon,
for one who intends to treat a practitioner,
they should first summon the spirits and ghosts and only then perform the treatment.
Each and every one was verified.
Furthermore, the practitioner should follow the illnesses of all sentient beings,
carefully weighing them through the scriptures and then inquiring with direct observation.
There is no dharma that does not lead to death.
World-Honored One, this morning I asked about its practice.
If a person performs this dharma, there will surely be efficacy below.
World-Honored One, for anyone wishing to practice the Dharma free from defilement,
they must first [purify themselves] and subsequently [perform the ritual] at every location where it is required.
World-Honored One, when performing ritual acts,
one need not discriminate between what is pure and what is impure according to one's whim;
simply act according to the mind.
Either in his own room where he sits or lies down,
or in another dwelling,
or within a Buddhist stūpa.
Whether in the midst of a wilderness or upon a pure mountain,
one may perform it in such various ways as the situation demands, according to the power of one's resolve, even amidst urgent circumstances.
That [specific] dharma will then be swiftly accomplished.
At times, one may go from a place where there are many people to a place where there are few people,
or even go alone by oneself.
Whether one has a wife and children or not—
none of these various circumstances pose any obstacle.
One should simply cultivate diligence in the mind and refrain from over-exhausting oneself with toil.
Within three days and nights, one will achieve accomplishment oneself;
one must simply recite the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
World-Honored One, it is only when a practitioner cultivates this dharma that this occurs.
I shall never be separated from that person.
I will ensure that the path they are shown does not lead them astray.
Furthermore, I will cause the ghosts and spirits to serve them so that they quickly gain strength and vigor.
May they cause those [beings] to penetrate the profound and spiritual manifestations,
knowing life and death;
may the dharmas they practice lead them swiftly beyond the mundane world.
World-Honored One, whenever one wishes to recite mantras or perform various ritual methods,
the recitation of the mantra and the summoning of spirits and deities must both be carried out in secret.
Do not allow them to make a sound.
When it is time to employ them, remember to summon them according to your will; do not hold them back.
If one clings to abiding, one must immediately purify it;
if one acts with coarseness, one must immediately practice subtlety.
[One should abandon] greed, anger, and delusion regarding fragrances.
"There are such obstacles to the Path that they would not allow a practitioner to cultivate it.
World-Honored One, those dharmas can be practiced and mastered by sentient beings in this defiled land."
Sentient beings in the Pure Land cultivate it,
yet those who are defiled by dust and grime fall into the three miserable realms.
World-Honored One, this matter does not transcend the four propositions.
If one simply gives rise to deep cultivation, there is nothing that will not be accomplished.
World-Honored One, furthermore, regarding the recitation of mantras, the robes one wears must not be mixed with others.
If one releases [the mantra] without interruption, it shall be obtained immediately upon wearing the garments on one's person.
With the exception of skins, furs, felt, and robes,
these do not belong to the category of items subject to formal ritual procedures;
all others may be accepted.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One established the methods for practitioners in varying degrees— whether many or few—
and whether they were those who had attained clear understanding or those who had not;
each was permitted to practice according to their own capacity.
What is undertaken will immediately be accomplished.
The spirit will manifest and speak with the practitioner, ensuring that success is attained.
This shall cause the practitioner to inquire about the directions for the distant path.
Knowing the various deeds of past lives and the present,
he announces them all in advance to human beings by name, swiftly employing them so that people may understand and be liberated.
The World-Honored One, a practitioner of the Dharma who knows the affairs of ten thousand years in the future,
perceives those afflicted by suffering, illness, and calamity;
he inscribes talismans and dispatches them so that they may travel a thousand li to bring recompense for the deceased.
If one writes [the mantra] on the forehead of a person who has been dead for one day, they will immediately return to life.
When performing this rite, if one writes it on the first day of the year, there is nothing that will not be accomplished.
On that day, one must write one thousand or two thousand copies.
This is for one year’s practice.
Its auspicious signs (*fu*)—from that day until this day—are of great efficacy.
The dates of the first year are not uniform.
In the Western Regions, the first day of the third month is taken as the beginning of the year;
in the Eastern land of the Han, the first month of the year is taken as the beginning of the year.
Each follows its own national custom in this regard.
If one asks what happens after these days have passed, the ritual signs (*liǎo*) lose their proper measure.
World-Honored One, these forty *liǎo* above, with the twenty *liǎo* for cultivating the spirit among them, are able to eliminate all decline and affliction.
The practitioner of this dharma cures the illnesses and sufferings of sentient beings.

Write one [character]... write it... swallow it or wear it; for all malignant diseases and malignant sores, write the talisman with vermilion and face it toward them, and they will immediately be cured.
World-Honored One, regarding all physical ailments of sentient beings— regardless of their type, distinctions, or severity—
once this has been inscribed upon a talisman, it will be effective immediately. Should it fail to take effect, [then know that it is not the fault of the Dharma].
Before the Tathāgata, I have cast off my bodhisattva body to take upon myself the suffering of sentient beings.
However, those who merely practice the Dharma must rely on this; for one who practices according to this Dharma, there shall be no [obstacles].
World-Honored One, the twenty talismans that follow will be able to eliminate [the calamities] within ten *yojanas*.
If a practitioner of the Dharma writes this out in vermilion and wears it for forty-one days,
they will possess great supernormal powers and attain the four kinds of unimpeded knowledge.
Transcending birth and death, they emerge from the mire.
The Buddhas praise them, and Bodhisattvas protect and mind them.
Within a hundred days, those who have externally associated with the five families shall all attain the realization of the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Each ascended into the air and departed.
Furthermore, when practitioners of the Dharma hold [the image] to their fifth finger joint, light radiates from it;
their bodies naturally become like pure lapis lazuli, transparent and radiant both inside and out.
In whatever country the practitioner dwells,
the king, princes, ministers, and the people will all submit to them;
as will all insects and beasts, whether flying or dwelling on land, including those with four legs.
All of them came bearing incense and flowers to make offerings.
The various devas scattered flowers and produced the sounds of great dharma music,
which reached far throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
"May all those who are hungry obtain the most excellent and sublime food and drink as offerings.
Having spoken these words, he immediately prepared various kinds of food and drink.
He went to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa,
prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times,
and then stood to one side and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, since time immemorial our families have constantly practiced the ten wholesome deeds; for what reason have we died today and yet again encountered the Tathāgata?
We pray that you will explain this for us and dispel our doubts."
At that time, the Tathāgata, in order to destroy [their delusions], explained these causes and conditions.
Upon hearing the Dharma, the elder and the others were filled with joy;
having long since attained arhatship, they rose into the air and departed.
At that time, the fourfold assembly stood in mid-air;
from the sky, they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and joyfully received and practiced [his teaching].

This *Dàodǐ qūcè guǐfù fǎshī* (The Great Path: The Whip and Spur for the Transmission of the Dharma Master) was written by the Preceptor Qingyou at the Śūraṅgama Monastery on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month in the first year of the Kwanji era, completed at the hour of Wei. In the autumn of the third year of the Heihō era, I had the manuscript from the Tōdai-ji (Katsuragi-san) collection copied by the scribe Takehara. As the original manuscript was damaged and difficult to read, I have corrected it using a superior copy.
